speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings following your tympanoplasty. To help me understand your current condition better, could you tell me how many days or weeks it has been since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of chronic ear infections and the new onset of shooting pain while eating along with sensitivity to earrings, are you experiencing any fluid drainage or a sensation of fullness in your ear currently?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Microscopic Examination reveals a healed tympanoplasty site on the right side with intact skin and no visible bulge, swelling, or active drainage in the ear canal. Post-Op Otoscopy images confirm normal post-surgical anatomy without signs of recurrent infection or granulation tissue.

speaker: Doctor

The microscopic examination and otoscopy images show a healed graft with no signs of infection or granulation tissue; since the pain is triggered by chewing and you have difficulty wearing earrings, does this pain radiate specifically to the jaw or temple area?

REQUEST TEST: TMJ_Special_Examination.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No jaw clicking heard. No tenderness with palpation of the mandibular area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the TMJ examination is normal and the ear canal appears healed, could you describe the exact location of the pain when you chew—is it strictly in the ear canal, or does it feel like it's coming from deep inside the bone?

Also, have you noticed any changes in the sensation of your jaw, such as numbness or tingling, or difficulty opening your mouth fully?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Superior Alveolar Nerve Neuroma (Post-Tympanoplasty).

The clinical picture of shooting pain triggered by chewing, combined with normal otoscopy and TMJ exam, strongly suggests the pain originates from the nerve itself (likely the superior alveolar nerve) rather than the ear or jaw joint. The difficulty wearing earrings may be a referred sensation or due to post-surgical nerve hypersensitivity. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the specific "shooting" quality and the exclusion of other causes.
